 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173 (1) OF MOTOR  VEHICLES ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED  31.01.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO.1171/2018 ON THE FILE OF THE  ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE  FIRST CLASS, RANEBENNUR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  -2-  MFA No. 100131 of 2023 PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. Compensation of Rs.2,87,760/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
The accident had occurred on 02.05.2018.
The accident is not disputed.
The liability of the insurer is also not disputed.

The claimant has suffered the following injuries:
i. fracture of distal end of radius left wrist, ii. fracture of scapula left side, thin subdural haematoma left basi temporal convexity 3.
Admittedly, the claimant is a coolie.
The claimant has suffered 24.4% disability as per the evidence given by the doctor.
The Tribunal has taken 20% disability to calculate the compensation towards loss of future income.
The Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.8,000/- p.m. in the absence of any proof relating to income.
The chart prepared by High Court Legal Services Committee, Dharwad would indicate that the notional income would b Rs.11,750/- p.m. for the accident which occurred in the year 2018.

entities.text: High Court Legal Services Committee, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, based on that the compensation has to be reassessed.
4. Since the insurer has admitted the liability, there is no difficulty in accepting the disability at 20%.

Hence, loss of future income would be Rs.11,750 income x 12 months x 11 multiplier x 20% disability = Rs.3,10,200/-
5.
The claimant was inpatient for 20 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and number of days he has spent as inpatient, this Court is of the view that compensation of Rs.15,000/- by the Tribunal is on lower side and Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded towards pain and suffering.
6. The compensation of Rs.49,060/- awarded under the head of medical expenses does not require any modification as the same is based on medical bills.

2 7.
Since the claimant was inpatient for 20 days, award of Rs.4,500/- towards attendant charges is on lower side and Rs.15,000/- is to be awarded.

8. Since the income is reassessed, the compensation towards loss of income during laid up period is to be reassessed by taking Rs.11,750/- as the monthly income and taking three months as laid up period given the fact that the claimant has suffered 24.4% disability to particular limb.

Rs.35,250/-
is awarded under the said head.
9. No compensation is awarded towards loss of amenities.
This Court is of the view that considering the disability suffered by the claimant, Rs.40,000/- has to be awarded under the said head.
10. In all, the claimant is entitled to Rs.4,89,510/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
11. Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation before the Tribunal within six weeks from today.
12. Appeal is allowed in part and the judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified as indicated above.
